claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have a child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 10 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 10 years old.

Now I need to ask you a few more questions to determine your eligibility:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now let me ask:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand your situation better.

**Do you make financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep (such as for food, clothes, pocket money, or accommodation)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out financially - I contribute towards his upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. To determine your eligibility, I need to understand more about your contributions.

**How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep, and how often do you make these contributions (for example, weekly, monthly, or in lump sums)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £20 a week towards his upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to ask:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure if anyone else is claiming for him at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Let me ask another important question:

**Who does Alex live with currently? For example, does he live with his other parent, a relative, or someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his other parent.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Now I need to understand the timeline:

**How long has Alex been living with his other parent? Is this a recent change, or has he been living there for a while?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been living with his other parent for quite a while now - it's been the arrangement for some time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask one more important question to complete my assessment:

**Has it been more than 8 weeks since Alex went to live with his other parent?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's been much longer than that - he's been living there for quite a while now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Assessment Complete

Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

Since Alex lives with his other parent and has been doing so for much longer than 8 weeks, the rules about children living with someone else apply to your situation. While you do contribute £20 per week towards Alex's upkeep, this amount is below the Child Benefit payment threshold (which is £25.60 per week for an eldest or only child).

According to the rules:
- You would normally get Child Benefit for 8 weeks after your child goes to live with someone else if nobody else claims
- After 8 weeks, payments could continue **only if** you contribute to your child's upkeep by an amount equal to or greater than the Child Benefit payment itself

Since your weekly contribution of £20 is less than the Child Benefit rate, and Alex has been living with his other parent for well over 8 weeks, you would not be eligible to claim.

Additionally, only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child, and typically this would be the person the child lives with - in this case, Alex's other parent.

If you wanted to become eligible in the future, you would need to either:
- Have Alex come to live with you, or
- Increase your contributions to at least match the Child Benefit rate (currently £25.60 per week)
